representation.prompts: Native HTML and KaTeX for every prompt with original wording, part labels, marks, bold emphasis, question-specific instructions and faithful vector figure crops. As in the earlier imports, printed captions such as "Figure 1" sit outside the crop; the alt text of each figure names it.
representation.solutions: Every question-specific mark-scheme page as ordered vector crops: working, marks, AOs, alternatives, special cases, examiner notes and diagrams. General marking pages and publisher pages are excluded.

cropMethod: PyMuPDF show_pdf_page clip to SVG with text as paths. Figure boxes snap to the drawing items wholly inside the caption region. Scheme page bounds cover all text spans, vector drawings and embedded images; breaks fall only in empty horizontal bands, preferring table rules and paragraph gaps; invisible white background fills are ignored when finding bands.
sourceNotes: Files were identified by their covers, not their names; the full inventory (SHA-256, page counts, pairing, duplicates) is on GitHub #124 and the release slice on #126.
The owner folders and the indexed PMT copies file the Core Pure papers as June 2020 and June 2021; the official mark schemes title them October 2020 and November 2021, so those are the sessions used.

October 2020 9FM0/01 and 9FM0/02 question paper covers print Monday 11 May 2020 and Thursday 14 May 2020; these are recorded verbatim as printed dates and no exam date is assigned. November 2021 9FM0/01 and 9FM0/02 covers print no date, so none is recorded; the paper list orders them by series.
October 2021 9MA0/01 and 9MA0/32 mark schemes are titled November 2021 on their covers; they pair by code and content with the October 2021 question papers, whose session is used.
October 2020 9MA0/02 mark scheme is titled Autumn 2020; it pairs by code and content with the October 2020 question paper.

Paper instructions are taken verbatim from each cover: the 2020-2021 Pure and Core Pure covers say "Inexact answers should be given to three significant figures unless otherwise stated"; Statistics covers add the statistical tables line; Mechanics covers give the g instruction, quoted on each Mechanics question.
October 2021 9MA0/32 Q4 prints its own bold instruction that g is modelled as 10 m s^-2; it is kept in the question.
October 2021 9MA0/31 Q2: the scatter diagram is printed on the continuation page (question paper page 5) and is placed after the sentence that refers to it.
Mid-page scheme starts (October 2020 9MA0/02 Q4, Q5 and Q9-Q16; October 2021 9MA0/32 Q5) are cut above the question header row, so every question carries only its own scheme.
mathsReview: Every question solved independently with SymPy and numeric checks (private scripts) and compared with the official scheme answers; no mathematical discrepancies and no source errors found.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: det M = 16 + 48 = 64 = k^2 so k = 8; cos theta = -1/2, sin theta = sqrt3/2 gives theta = 120; area of S is 2a^2 so area of S' = 64 x 2a^2 = 128a^2. Agrees with scheme.

cos^2(x/3) = 1 - x^2/9 + x^4/243; integral of 1/x - x/9 + x^3/243 from pi/6 to pi/2 = 0.98295; calculator 0.98280; the approximation is accurate to 3 decimal places (2 s.f. agreement). Agrees with scheme.
Substituting x = (w + 1)/4 and matching coefficients with w^3 - 9w^2 - 97w + c gives a = 4, b = -12, c = 105. Agrees with scheme.

AB is possible (2 columns match 2 rows); A + B is not (different dimensions); the product is 5I with a = 1, b = 2, lambda = 5, so the inverse is (1/5) of the second matrix; det M = sin theta sin 2theta - cos theta cos 2theta = -cos 3theta = 0 gives theta = pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6. Agrees with scheme.
Integral of 2e^(-x/2) from 1 to infinity = 4e^(-1/2); mean = (1/24) integral from 0 to 24 = 8; a higher actual mean means increasing the constant 8. Agrees with scheme.

(2, 3, -4) is perpendicular to both direction vectors; 2x + 3y - 4z = 7; |2(4 + t) + 3(-5 + 6t) - 4(2 - 3t) - 7|/sqrt29 = 2 sqrt29 gives t = 5/2 or -9/8: A = (13/2, 10, -11/2) or (23/8, -47/4, 43/8). Agrees with scheme.

Volume stays 30 litres so red leaves at 3r/30: dr/dt = 2 - r/10, alpha = 10; r = 20 - 10e^(-t/10); equal amounts when r = 15, t = 10 ln 2 = 7 s; the model over-predicts the rate (7 s against 9 s observed). Agrees with scheme.

x = cosh u gives the integral of cosh^2 u = (1/2)(x sqrt(x^2 - 1) + arcosh x) + k (derivative check zero for x > 1); integration by parts of (4/15) x arcosh x from 1 to 3 = (1/15)(17 ln(3 + 2 sqrt2) - 6 sqrt2) = 1.4321. Agrees with scheme.

questions.mathsCheckpoint: |z1 z2| = 3 sqrt2, arg(z1 z2) = pi/3 - pi/12 = pi/4; arg(w^n) = n pi/4 = 0 (mod 2pi) gives n = 8, |w^8| = (3 sqrt2)^8 = 104 976. Agrees with scheme.
An invariant line y = mx + c maps to itself only if 2m^2 - m + 5 = 0, whose discriminant is 1 - 40 = -39 < 0, so there are no real m and no invariant lines. Agrees with scheme.
arcsin x = x + x^3/6 + ...; x = 1/2 gives pi/6 = 1/2 + 1/48 = 25/48, so pi = 25/8. Agrees with scheme.
Sum of (2r - 1)^3 = 8 sum r^3 - 12 sum r^2 + 6 sum r - n = n^2(2n^2 - 1) (checked n = 1 to 4); S(n + 10) - S(n) = 99 800 gives n = 5, so the smallest number is 11. Agrees with scheme.

dy/dx = -1/sqrt(4 - x^2) is never 0; at x = 1 the normal has gradient sqrt3 through (1, pi/3): A = (1 - sqrt3 pi/9, 0), B = (0, pi/3 - sqrt3); area = (1/54)(27 sqrt3 - 18 pi + sqrt3 pi^2): p = 27, q = -18, r = 1. Agrees with scheme.

dx/dtheta = -a sin theta (p + 4 cos theta) = 0 needs cos theta = -p/4 with two solutions, so 2 < p < 4 (four vertical tangents); a dimpled limacon; cross-section area (1/2) integral of 400(3 + 2cos theta)^2 = 4400 pi cm^2, volume 1 244 071 cm^3, time = 1244.07/50 = 25 minutes; e.g. the sides are not vertical. Agrees with scheme.
sinh((1/2) ln 3) = (sqrt3 - 1/sqrt3)/2 = 1/sqrt3; V = pi integral of sinh^2 y from 0 to (1/2) ln 3 = (pi/4)(4/3 - ln 3). Agrees with scheme.

|6 + 6i| = 6 sqrt2, arg pi/4; other vertices 6 sqrt2 e^(i theta) with theta = 13pi/20, -19pi/20, -11pi/20, -3pi/20; region inside the circle centre 2i radius 2 between the half-lines; area = (1/2) integral of (4 sin theta)^2 from pi/4 to pi/3 = pi/3 + 2 - sqrt3. Agrees with scheme.

Sum = 1/(1 - z); with z = (1/2)e^(i theta), Im = 2 sin theta/(5 - 4 cos theta), which is the given series; Re = 2(2 - cos theta)/(5 - 4 cos theta) > 0 for all theta, so the sum cannot be purely imaginary. Agrees with scheme.

log T = b log l + log a; b = 0.45/0.91 = 0.495, log a = 0.346, a = 2.22: T = 2.22 l^0.495; a is the time of one swing of a 1 m pendulum. Agrees with scheme.
f has maximum (3k/2, k), meets the axes at (0, -2k), (k, 0), (2k, 0); k - |2x - 3k| > x - k for k < x < 5k/3: {x : k < x < 5k/3}; minimum of 3 - 5f(x/2) at (3k, 3 - 5k). Agrees with scheme.
